title: Agencies request comment on proposed rules to strengthen capital requirements for large banks
summary: The Federal Reserve, FDIC, and OCC jointly released a Basel III endgame proposal on July 27, 2023, seeking public comment through November 30, 2023. The proposal would apply to banks with $100 billion or more in total assets and is estimated to result in an aggregate 16 percent increase in common equity tier 1 capital requirements for affected bank holding companies. The new framework would begin transitioning on July 1, 2025, with full compliance required by July 1, 2028.
key_points: Proposal applies to banks with $100 billion or more in total assets; community banks are excluded
Estimated 16 percent aggregate increase in common equity tier 1 capital requirements for affected bank holding companies
Proposed changes would standardize credit risk, market risk, operational risk, and financial derivative risk measurements
Banks would be required to include unrealized gains and losses from certain securities in capital ratios
Transition to new framework begins July 1, 2025, with full compliance required by July 1, 2028
Federal Reserve also proposed adjustments to the GSIB surcharge calculation, measuring systemic importance averaged over the full year instead of only at year-end
why_it_matters: This regulatory proposal represents the final components of the Basel III international capital framework and would meaningfully increase capital buffers for large banks. The 16 percent CET1 increase would reduce risk-weighted asset flexibility and could constrain lending capacity or require capital raises for the most affected institutions. The phased implementation provides time for adaptation, but banks must plan for higher capital requirements affecting their business models.
market_structure_context: The proposal modifies the capital framework for large banks, affecting how banks measure and hold capital against credit risk, market risk, operational risk, and financial derivative risk. It also introduces the supplementary leverage ratio and the countercyclical capital buffer for covered banks, and modifies GSIB surcharge calculation methodology.
important_numbers: $100 billion asset threshold for covered banks
